chok-yaakov/1:ח: And not any pottery vessel used hot — such is Tur's language; and Beit Yosef explained his intent: even if one did not use it except in kli sheini — heating does not help for it; and so Rambam in chapter 5 of Laws of Chametz equates a pottery vessel used in kli sheini to using it in kli rishon, for it has no remedy — until here; and if so the Mechaber appears to me to have copied here Tur's language — his intent to forbid even in kli sheini, like the Rav's view in the gloss; but Rabbeinu Moshe in Darkei Moshe wrote: according to Tur it does not absorb except through kli rishon or via pouring; but kli sheini not — not like Beit Yosef — until here; and so it was necessary to emend here on the Mechaber's language which is Tur's language; and one says: even in kli sheini; and it is simple. chok-yaakov/2:ב: And if they filled it with coals from inside — it is permitted. Indeed in Shibulei Leket general rule 7 siman 58 and in Sefer Tanya they wrote, and these are his words: and bocheya — and it is like a thin griddle — it is forbidden to bake with it on Pesach — what is the reason? Its heating is from outside. And if it is full and they heated it from inside — it is permitted — such as a pottery griddle whose way is to heat it from inside and bake a cake beneath it — since the heating is from inside it is like an oven — end of his words. And so too Kol Bo daf 50 side d, and these are his words: perhaps he is concerned for them lest they crack — and it is not comparable to a pottery griddle (and they call the bocheya in the Talmud biv, following Rambam's language chapter 5 law 22 who wrote thus — see there) that we wrote that if they filled it with coals and its heating that one uses with it — there its heating is from inside, whereas if its heating is from outside — if they heat it from inside they do not heat it properly because he is concerned for them since they commonly crack — end of his words. Behold it is explicitly clear from their words that also in a bocheya heating from inside does not help unless in that bocheya whose way is to heat from inside (and even Kol Bo's language can be strained and interpreted somewhat another way — nevertheless Shibulei Leket and Tanya's language cannot be interpreted except as I wrote) — and it appears they followed in this the text versions of Rif and Rosh chapter Kol Sha'ah that we read in the Talmud: and if it is full and its heating from inside it is considered proper — if so; and according to this text it is seemingly difficult, for it is duplicated language — full means heating from inside; therefore they explain that this is what it means: and if it is full — that is, in that bocheya that they heated from inside it is considered proper; and per their words the sugya of the Talmud will be well settled and one need not strain and say that a bocheya is different as Beit Yosef wrote. And I extended in all this even though for the law it is possible they do not disagree — they do not deal with a bocheya made of bricks and clay, for it is possible all agree that those made of bricks and clay we wrote not concerned lest they crack — and their dispute is in the explanation of the bocheya in the Talmud — nevertheless I extended to explain the matters because I saw that Beit Yosef toiled to strain and resolve Rashba's words and after him the Acharonim followed to question his words and Tiyul Yoreh De'ah's words — and in truth there is not even a bit of difficulty here, for all the matters are taken from the sugya of the Talmud explicitly — and this requires further study in Rashba's own words and in Tiyul Yoreh De'ah there — and here in Orach Chayyim it appears per the Mechaber's view and he would explain Rosh's words per their plain sense and did not wish to be precise in the language "and they heated it from inside" — and it is simple.

But here, since there was no known chametz in them — only a general concern — therefore he ruled that hagalah helps — and it is straightforward.
chok-yaakov/11:א: It is permitted via hagalah. And Taz wrote in the name of Rosh: specifically in an oven in which chametz was baked without liquid — libun is required — but not a griddle — for we are not concerned lest the oil dried and the chametz was baked without liquid, because there is still moisture of liquid there — and the same law applies to a metal pot in which they cook — end of his words. And in Yoreh De'ah siman 121 the Mechaber wrote: even though for Pesach hagalah suffices — for other prohibitions libun is required — and his reason: since there are many views regarding a griddle that it is not like use via fire — hagalah suffices — therefore we rely on them regarding chametz, for there are poskim who hold permitted absorption is called — as written in notes 14 and 22 — and not like Eliyah Rabbah who left the Mechaber's words as requiring further study. Also in Pri Chadash Yoreh De'ah siman 121 note 8 he criticized Shach and Taz — and according to what is written everything is well resolved — examine what is written in the name of responsum Maharam of Padua siman 96 — another distinction between a year-round griddle and regarding Pesach — see there.
chok-yaakov/11:ב: However hagalah suffices for it — and so they practice. And Magen Avraham wrote: and those molds in which they bake cakes — libun is required.
chok-yaakov/12:_: One should not forbid b'dieved. The reason: we do not say that its absorption travels throughout it — and even if its absorption travels — nevertheless it is like two distinct vessels — and so too it is explained in Yoreh De'ah from Tur's and Beit Yosef's words and rulings of Maharai siman 131. And also in Pri Chadash there note 15 he extended to prove thus — even l'chatchila it is permitted to kasher part of it during the year — only on Pesach one should be stringent l'chatchila — because Bach wrote it is impossible that matzah did not also absorb chametz taste during the year via kli rishon when they rinse them to clean from filth — and so too in Pri Chadash there note 16 that such is the primary view. And b'dieved one should not forbid even if one inserted it into the food with one's hands — because we do not establish a prohibition — and like two distinct vessels — as the Rav ruled explicitly there in Yoreh De'ah — and even in doubt one should permit b'dieved — as Ohel Leah wrote explicitly general rule 58 law 21 in the name of Tiyul Yoreh De'ah — and all this is not like the implication of Taz and Magen Avraham — examine their words and be precise.
chok-yaakov/13:א: Tela'im. Every tela in this seif — that is, what was fixed by nails — but what was made via fusion of lead or iron and silver and other kinds of metal — since it was made via fusion in fire and became one body — it is preferable to libun, for it is as if made anew — such is the agreement of the Acharonim. And vessels that are coated with tin — such as copper vessels that they have in the land of Turkey — Ra'ah volume 1 siman 43 writes that hagalah is not required, since they coat it with tin — examine in Shaarei Deah who extended to bring disputing views on this — and wrote that indeed some gedolim of the land are stringent upon themselves — and in any case it appears good in the eyes of God and man to immerse it after tin coating without a blessing — end of his words. And in Pri Chadash Orach Chayyim he ruled that hagalah is required after tin coating — and so they practice in Jerusalem — see cursorily.
chok-yaakov/13:ב: Or one places coals on the place of the tela until the body of the prohibition is burned. And then — even though forbidden absorption preceded — it is permitted, since the place of the tela was whitened — as the implication of Rashba's language in responsum siman 371 — and the Mechaber — and so too Levush. And Bach wrote on Rashba: it appears to me that where forbidden absorption preceded — libun of the place of the tela does not help — and I do not know whence Bach came to explain thus — on the contrary, Rashba's implication is that in every case where the chametz beneath the tela was burned — it suffices. And as stated above — the primary view is not like Bach. And in Shach and Magen Avraham I saw that they adopt as primary Bach's words and wonder at Shulchan Aruch's language here — and all this was caused them because when they copied Bach's words they also copied what Bach concluded — and so too Ohel Leah general rule 58 law 19 — and they understood that it refers to this law — and therefore they adopted his words for halachic ruling. And in truth I examined well in Ohel Leah there and I did not see any decision from his words for this law — and Bach did not write "and so too Ohel Leah" — only on the end of his language that he concluded: for fire burns everything — and what remains in it now will never emit — and this Ohel Leah wrote there explicitly — see there. And if it was whitened thus or one removed the tela'im once — after hagalah it is again permitted to kasher thus with the tela each time — since it is no longer called preceded forbidden absorption for the tela. And all this is when the tela is well attached in a manner that there is no crack and groove between the body of the vessel and the tela — for if not, even before the tela one requires libun or to remove the tela or to widen the crack so one can scrape it — and it is straightforward — and so is the agreement of the Acharonim.
chok-yaakov/13:ג: And one scrapes them well. And if it is impossible to scrape — one places coals upon it as above.
chok-yaakov/14:א: That they cover the pot with it. He wrote thus to exclude that cover upon which they bake dough — which requires libun — as Beit Yosef wrote to explain thus Mordechai's view in chapter 21 that libun is required in a cover. Indeed according to what Ohel Leah wrote general rule 58 law 26 in the name of Mordechai — it implies that in an ordinary pot cover libun is required — and one should not deviate from Shulchan Aruch's ruling — and especially on Pesach, for permitted absorption is called — as written above note 14.
chok-yaakov/14:ב: All the food is forbidden. Per the Mechaber's view above siman 447 that nat bar nat l'pagam is permitted on Pesach — it must be that here we deal where it is still ben yomo that was used orally — or it must be per the practice to forbid in a cover even though it is not ben yomo — as explained in Beit Yosef siman 473.
chok-yaakov/16:א: To libun the mortar. And specifically regarding chametz on Pesach — unlike all other days of the year in a forbidden mortar and the like — according to all hagalah suffices — and so too in the hagahah Eshel Avraham end of chapter HaSocher et haPo'el in the name of Rabbenu Tam — and in responsum Maharam of Rotenburg siman 447 — and Kol Bo — and Tosefta — however this requires further study: from all the poskim's words regarding knives and spits it implies that there is more reason to be lenient to kasher regarding Pesach — and other prohibitions require libun — and so too it is explained there from Rabbenu Tam's own words. And it is possible that specifically here regarding the mortar they were stringent because it is common to grind in it fat and onions with bread crumbs — which is a sharp thing like sourdough according to Rashi — and libun was required, as explained in Tur — unlike a forbidden mortar where there is concern only for forbidden fat that one does not customarily grind in it with sharp things — therefore hagalah suffices — and so it implies somewhat in Kol Bo — see there.
chok-yaakov/17:ב: Even via hagalah. In Tosefta siman 131 it is explained that even if one wants to peel it with a craft tool and kasher it afterward — it also does not help — and so too it implies in Mahariv siman 193. And the reason: because it is impossible to scrape it properly. And for this reason too one does not kasher vessels in which there was always flour or chametz liquids and the like (and the law of kashering barrels will be explained nearby) — and this is specifically of wood — unlike metal and pewter vessels, where they practice to kasher in every case. Indeed if they held water in it before Pesach for some time — it is permitted to kasher it — and such is the agreement of the Acharonim.
chok-yaakov/18:א: Not to use a sieve via hagalah — but one must buy new ones. And if one transgressed and sifted with it via good rubbing in hagalah — one should not forbid even during Pesach — since according to Kol Bo and the Mechaber even l'chatchila it suffices in such a case — it is fit to rely on it b'dieved for a slight prohibition. But l'chatchila one should not use it — only buy new ones. And so too where water came upon the sieve that they did not rub it well first — even on part of it — it has no remedy to use it on Pesach — Maharil. And Magen Avraham wrote, and these are his words: and it appears to me that even in a place where there is no new sieve — it is better not to sift the flour — end of his words. And I do not know whence this law came to him — for our eyes see that every flour that was not sifted has several broken and whole grains — and the matzah or dough is forbidden, as explained below siman 467. And this sieve b'dieved — good rubbing and hagalah help for it — all the more so if one sifted before Pesach that was nullified — and it is not called nullifying a prohibition l'chatchila, since it is still the time of permission and a slight doubt in general — therefore it appears to me that in a time of pressure it is correct to do so even l'chatchila — for every time of pressure is considered like b'dieved. And if one transgressed and kneaded the dough and did not sift the flour — it is possible to forbid the entire dough — for the matter is known that every flour that was not sifted commonly has broken and whole grains in them — as several times an incident came before us. And I was asked regarding one who said according to his innocence that his way is to wash well after Pesach the sieve in order to preserve it for the coming year — and he sifted flour in it for Pesach — and I permitted what he sifted in it b'dieved and to rely on good rubbing as the Mechaber's view. And further: even if we say that residue remained stuck because he did not rub well and it became mixed within the flour (and see Eliyah Rabbah siman 453 and 466 that separation within flour returns and is shaken) — even though he sifted the flour during Pesach — nevertheless it was already explained above siman 447 that hard chametz is nullified in sixty even during Pesach — since there is only concern for some crumb that remained stuck from the past year, which is hard chametz — and it is nullified as stated.
chok-yaakov/18:ג: All the stitches. That is — also what is at the edge of the bag, which is the imrah — and so too it implies there in Tosefta from the proof of chapter Dam haNidah — see there. And Magen Avraham wrote: and so one should practice with cloths that they make matzah upon. If one wants to use them a second time — what they flip them does not help — for chametz bursts through and goes from side to side — rather one must untie the stitches and launder well — end of his words. And with this it is possible that one need not untie the imrah — because they do not make matzot on the imrah — only in the middle of the cloth. And if one transgressed b'dieved and made matzah on the sheet without laundering at all — if it is during Pesach — even b'dieved one should forbid. But if one flipped the sheet or laundered it — even though he did not untie the stitches — one should not be stringent b'dieved — it appears to me. And so too regarding bags: if they laundered and did not untie the stitches and put flour inside — one should not forbid b'dieved. And see Eliyah Rabbah siman 453 note 21 what is written there.
chok-yaakov/19:_: That hagalah does not help for it — because its use is via fire. And Taz wrote: the Pesach sifter that one preserves for the coming year — it needs no kashering for another year — and one who is stringent to kasher it did not act well — for he will come to err to kasher a chametz sifter — only scrape it well — end of his words. And his words appear correct — unlike what Magen Avraham wrote in the name of Darkei Moshe in the name of Mahariv that hagalah is required — and Magen Avraham wrote: and it also does not help if one peels the sifter and kasher's it. And if one took matzah in a sifter that is used all year — if it is clean, peeling the matzah suffices; and if it is not clean — since they use upon it all year cakes with fat — the whole thing is forbidden. And if they dropped sour matzah in it and afterward dropped other matzot in it — they all require peeling. And he wrote in Sefer Epi Rabbeinu in introduction 70: if one removed sour matzah with a mirror and afterward dropped others in it and the first ones became mixed with the last ones — they were nullified — end of his words. And this is a rejected reasoning — for he holds that there is no prohibition of absorbed substance emitted from a vessel without gravy — and there is prohibition only in the first bread because there was a bit visible — and if it became mixed it is nullified. But we hold that a vessel emits without gravy — end of his words — Magen Avraham. And my brother-in-law the Rav R' Efrayim may he live long resolved: Epi Rabbeinu's intent is not upon those matzot that they took in it afterward that the first ones taken immediately after the sour matzah should be nullified — as Magen Avraham understood — rather "first ones" — his intent is what they took before they took the sour matzah, which became mixed with what they took afterward. And he aimed well in this — even though it appears to me that Epi Rabbeinu's language pushes Magen Avraham — for since he mentions that the first ones became mixed with the last ones — it implies the last ones are the majority of the permitted — as the Talmud is precise in chapter Elu haNisrafim regarding those stoned in burning. Nevertheless one should not be so precise in the poskim's words to reject their words on this basis — and examine further in Magen Avraham who extended on this matter of nullification. And in my humble opinion all these matters were said only for one who holds dry in dry — one in two is nullified regarding Pesach — but according to what was explained above siman 447 that dry in dry is not nullified on Pesach — and even six or more — nevertheless it returns and is shaken during Pesach whenever it was not mixed wet with wet — and it is forbidden to eat them during Pesach, since the prohibition is visible within them — as explained in Magen Avraham's own words in siman 458 — see there. If so — the law of nullification does not apply here at all — only to feed them to a child orally and the like. And Magen Avraham concluded further, and these are his words: and it appears to me that all this deals with matzah that became fully leavened chametz — but doubled and bloated matzah — since it is itself a mere stringency, as written siman 461 — it suffices to forbid the sifter l'chatchila — but not to forbid the other matzot — end of his words. And greater than this I saw with my teacher the Gaon Maharsh, and these are his words: he did not forbid the sifter when asked before him about bloated or doubled matzah — from the reason it appears to me it is considered like a deed — for one will not escape in most bakings that one of them will not be forbidden because of bloated or doubled — and each time a new sifter will be needed — also the oven will be forbidden and require heating again — and the like — the Torah spared the money of Israel. And further: behold Kol Bo is brought in Beit Yosef in this siman — he ruled that if one placed dry matzah — even hot — on a chametz vessel, or even on hot chametz bread — it does not forbid from it at all — and he brought thus as practical halachah. And he wrote further there on a chametz sifter, and these are his words: it is possible that if one scrubs it much and heats it inside the oven — it is permitted — like two distinct vessels — and even though we do not hold like him — nevertheless with bloated and doubled, which is itself a mere stringency — let us not add upon it — and we do not forbid the sifter even l'chatchila — and so practices after him my teacher the Gaon R' Wolf may he live long. And "one must buy a new one" etc. — the author of Imrei Noam wrote in responsum siman 5: an incident occurred where they baked matzot before Pesach in a sifter and they were uncertain whether it was new or old that chametz was used in it — all agree that in these matzot there is no concern of chametz prohibition — end of his words.
chok-yaakov/20:_: Because sometimes the broth spills. But without this reason — even though they store hot chametz in it — there is nothing in this — since they place it with the vessels in which there is chametz — and it does not absorb anything, since there is the interruption of the vessel — therefore the reason that broth spilled upon it was needed. And this is the intent of Haggahat Maimoni that Beit Yosef brought — and he returned here from what he brought in Beit Yosef to explain Haggahat's words on another matter — and so Bach agreed to the law. And Mahariv siman 193 ruled that pouring does not help — since sometimes they place peshtida upon it — only kasher them via a glowing stone and pouring. And the Acharonim wrote further in the name of Maharil: that even after hagalah — if anything spilled upon it on Pesach — do not lift them at all; and even after hagalah do not use upon them anything hot except via the interruption of cloths — and all this is extreme stringencies — for the stringency of hagalah suffices — and so they practice. And Taz siman 452 wrote, and these are his words: women practice not to use on Pesach a pot into which boiling water was spilled on the stone with which they kasher it — from the reason that the smell of chametz entered it — and there is no smell and no taste — for there is no prohibition at all on Pesach — end of his words. And see in my Minchat Yehudah general rule 53 note 12 — it appears there are two reasons to forbid — from the law of the Talmud l'chatchila and the custom of Israel is Torah — however b'dieved it certainly does not forbid.
chok-yaakov/21:ג: And b'dieved if they put wine in them. Thus wrote Mordechai: that the taste of beer is nullified in sixty before Pesach and does not return and is shaken on Pesach — and one should not be stringent to measure in all the barrels because we do not know how much emits from it — for this case is different here, for permitted absorption is called — therefore we measure according to what it was emitting and was nullified in sixty. And further: everything absorbed is included as nitelaf — also beer in wine is nitelaf — end of his words. And in truth the first reason is very puzzling — for even if we say that the primary view is per the poskim that chametz is called permitted absorption — nevertheless what of it? Since we do not know how much emits from it — certainly we measure against the entirety — for behold regarding meat in milk — which is also called permitted absorption — nevertheless when inserting a milking spoon into a pot of meat, or the reverse — for everyone we measure against the entirety — because we do not know how much emits from it — what difference to me forbidden absorption or permitted absorption? Therefore it appears to me the primary view is not to be lenient except for the second reason: according to what we hold, nat ta'am l'pagam is forbidden on Pesach — if so, one should not be lenient except to pour from it before Pesach into a Pesach barrel — and so too Magen Avraham note 40. And specifically in wine where the beer imparts taste l'pagam — but in mead water one should not be lenient unless the barrels are not ben yomo (but in a sharp wine vessel — even if it is not ben yomo — it is forbidden) — Magen Avraham — examine there.
chok-yaakov/22:א: Beit se'or — it is the vessel in which they make se'or to leaven the dough in it. And the Rav already wrote above in siman 452 seif 11 — and examine in this siman seif 16 that all kneading vessels — they practice to plaster them with mud or to give them to a gentile.
chok-yaakov/22:ב: And beit charoset — that is, they put sharp things with chametz in it. And examine in Taz who wonders on the Rav who ruled here anonymously like the Mechaber's view that hagalah suffices for it — and in seif 16 regarding the mortar that libun is specifically required — it should be learned from the law of beit se'or and charoset. And he answered: that case is different there, for we deal with a metal mortar — since libun is possible — unlike here where we deal with wood and pewter vessels where libun is impossible — end of his words. And I did not arrive at the end of his view — for in the mortar above the Rav wrote explicitly that if it is of wood it has no remedy with hagalah alone — rather one must peel it with a craft tool and kasher it. And in my humble opinion initially this requires further study: one — it is possible that Rama himself relied that beit charoset is comparable to beit se'or — which is a kneading vessel and requires plastering with mud — as written in note 59. And examine Eliyah Rabbah: above we deal where one wants to return and grind in the mortar on Pesach sharp things as is his custom — therefore they are more stringent — unlike here where he does not want to use it during Pesach for its first use with a sharp thing — only other things. And proof for this: it is comparable to beit se'or — for certainly one does not use se'or or chametz in it during Pesach — and it is simple.
chok-yaakov/22:ג: But cold — examine what the Rav wrote above in seif 1 in the hagahah and what is written there.
chok-yaakov/22:ה: And the oven of the winter house — the agreement of the Acharonim is that b'dieved the dish cooked in it is permitted — and so too it appears to me the primary view — that it should be only like two pots that do not absorb from one to the other — as explained in Taz Yoreh De'ah siman 92 note 29 — and examine in my Minchat Yehudah general rule 55 note 22. And so too if it is a time of pressure where it is impossible otherwise — it is considered like b'dieved. And in any case — one should scrub the oven well on all sides and heat it well — and afterward plaster with mud the place of the pot's seat to the thickness of a finger. But if one baked matzah in it without a dividing screen — one should forbid even b'dieved. Indeed in Levush it implies that one should permit via good heating even l'chatchila — since they heated it from inside (and one need not heat the entire oven full of wood — only the place where they customarily heat all year and the place of the pot's seat — like two distinct vessels; and some say regarding an oven in which they bake that we require coals to go over its entire face — for its way is to heat it entirely — and the same if one bakes in this oven — and it is simple) — and so I brought in my Minchat Yehudah general rule 60 — for such appears to me the primary view — and see what is written above note 9. But who will be lenient regarding a matter on which the Acharonim agreed — also my teacher the Maharsh was stringent in the matter, as my brother-in-law the Rav wrote in Shulchan Aruch — therefore one should not be lenient to bake matzah in it in any case. And nevertheless — in great monetary loss and prevention of Yom Tov joy — one should permit b'dieved and in a time of pressure even l'chatchila. And regarding the oven from outside — one should permit simply via plastering with mud to the thickness of a finger.
chok-yaakov/25:ב: However there are those who are stringent. And Magen Avraham wrote in note 59, and these are his words: and Agudah wrote — vessels whose use is cold, such as bottles and cups — it is better to kasher via pouring than to kasher them together with vessels whose use is hot — end of his words. And Tur and the Mechaber already wrote above seif 9 and in siman 452 that one who kasher's before five hours — there is no practical difference in all this. And it is possible that for this reason the custom spread in these countries to kasher all the vessels first via a glowing stone — and afterward they return and kasher them all together in a yorah. And nevertheless in the first hagalah it does not work — since they do it via water mixed with earth, as explained below siman 452 — also they do it when the vessels are still dirty — for hagalah does not help when chametz is in visible presence.
beur-hagra/1:ג: And it is good to lock them etc. — at the end of the chapter in Rosh and Tur as written there 6:1 regarding chametz of Eretz Yisrael etc., and even if he did not accept responsibility that one need not destroy it, as written in siman 450 seif 2, and the same law applies here; see Bach:
beur-hagra/1:ד: And not to place etc. even etc. — there and there, and as written in Zevachim 95b, the Torah said asher etc.:
beur-hagra/1:ה: And there are those who forbid. — Rambam in chapter 5 according to his view, since in other vessels hagalah is required as Rif, Rambam, and all poskim wrote, and they learned from what is written at the end of Avodah Zarah that items used in them with hot water etc., and all the more so for those who hold kli sheini absorbs from that in Chullin 8b as written in siman 447 seif 3 in the gloss, and we say in Zevachim there — it absorbs without cooking etc., and in Yerushalmi chapter 1 of Maaser and chapter 3 of Shabbat — there, a pottery vessel absorbs, and so too Rif and Rosh, as written in seif 5 regarding and if their use etc.; but there is no such thing — they did not write except regarding bowls whose use is via pouring — to kasher also via pouring, as Tosafot wrote in Shabbat that these certainly require kashering as above, and this is what Taz wrote 'rather, if one poured etc.' and so too Re'em at the beginning of Laws of Pesach — between bowls into which one poured boiling water; but the Mechaber's words in seif 5 are wondrous and are only according to Rashba — see siman 447 seif 3 in the gloss and Magen Avraham:
beur-hagra/1:ט: Every vessel. — Pesachim 30b: all vessels in which chametz was used cold, one may use matzah cold, except for a yeast container etc.; such is the text of the Rishonim, and Mordechai wrote — not that use in hot is forbidden, but because of the end regarding a yeast container: even if one used it cold, since its chametz is hard it is as though one used it hot, and it is forbidden to use even cold; and the same law applies to every vessel whose use is in hot, lest one come to use it hot; and so too Ran also from that of a yeast container as above, except that he explained that in the first clause it is forbidden to use in hot, and so too Rambam, except that Ran wrote specifically regarding chametz because it is sharp like yayin nesech, and Magen Avraham wrote that it mentions 'one uses cold' — not that use in hot is forbidden, but to exclude that if one used it in hot, even cold use is forbidden; and Ran wrote that therefore they said regarding pots on Pesach — break them; and in Chullin 111b regarding that pan etc.; except that Ran and Magen Avraham wrote specifically regarding pottery vessels, as the text of Rif, Rambam, and the Geonim: all pottery vessels etc., and the reason is because it has no remedy through kashering one comes to forget, and thereby one comes to use in hot; and Rosh does not have the text 'cold' and permits even in hot — see above siman 122, and here he ruled according to Mordechai's text which reads 'all vessels etc.' and according to his explanation, and so too in Yoreh De'ah siman 121 seif 5 in the gloss, except that he wrote specifically in a fixed manner, but in an occasional manner it is permitted, as written at the end of Avodah Zarah and we consult etc. and to cut cold with it; but if one used it cold, it is permitted even in hot for all texts — this explains even according to Rambam and Ran, see in Milchamot; and even in pottery vessels — as Ran wrote specifically regarding chametz because it is sharp like yayin nesech — if one puts it away for storage, and even if one does not put it away for storage but it is pottery and its initial use was with yayin nesech, it is forbidden as written in Avodah Zarah 33, see there; but for other prohibitions, no; and so too in Yoreh De'ah siman 121 seif 5 in the gloss, except that he was stringent regarding other vessels if there is concern that sometimes it was used in hot, since kashering is possible; and all this is with rinsing, but without rinsing it is certainly forbidden as written at the end of Avodah Zarah: items used in them cold — rinse them etc., and even to use them cold, as written in Chullin 'cold in cold is permitted' etc.; and there 111b: a knife with which one slaughtered etc., and we hold as one who says rinsing is required, and the knife is the subject as Rosh wrote at the beginning of Chullin siman 10, see there; and even though it did not absorb at all as written 8b regarding permitted absorption etc.; and likewise a treif knife to slaughter with — even according to one who says cold requires rinsing, and specifically a knife fit for slaughtering is permitted; and Tosafot there s.v. knife; and all this is in a moist item, but in a dry item it is permitted, as written in siman 91 seif 2 in the gloss, and Tosafot Avodah Zarah 32a s.v. and the etc.:
beur-hagra/2:ב: And likewise. — Tur according to R' Yonah:
beur-hagra/3:א: Seif 3 — knives we kasher. — Gemara there; and in the first chapter of Chullin 8b a knife requires libun, and so in Tosefta Avodah Zarah: spits, skewers, and knives — one whitens them in fire; Rabbenu Tam explained in Tosafot Chullin there s.v. that was whitened, and at the end of Avodah Zarah 76b s.v. he said to distinguish between chametz which absorbs permitted and other prohibitions which absorb prohibited, as he distinguished; and there in Gemara regarding spits and skewers, see there; and Ran wrote that such is Raavad's view, and Magen Avraham wrote that such is Rambam's view — that in Laws of Chametz he wrote knives through hagalah, and in Pesachim 37. Magen Avraham wrote through libun, and therefore in Laws of Chametz he omitted that spits and skewers require libun, for according to his view they too are through hagalah, and it is not his way to write what is not explicit in Gemara; and further Rabbenu Tam explained there and there to distinguish between a small knife and a large knife on which one roasts meat and whose use is via fire, and he brings proof from Yerushalmi end of Avodah Zarah: a knife — thrust it three times in the ground and it suffices; R' Bun in the name of R' Yehudah — this that you might say regarding a small knife, but regarding a large knife it requires libun; and Tosafot rejected his proof from Yerushalmi — it deals with cutting cold with it, and cold — there is no distinction between their use via fire or via hot, rather he explained that a large knife is apt to have crevices, and therefore neither scraping nor hagalah helps; and R' Baruch reconciled the proof, see there; and accordingly one may say there is no distinction between chametz and other prohibitions, and so too Rif and Rosh in chapter Kol Sha'ah who brought the baraita of spits and skewers regarding chametz; and Ran wrote that such is Ramban's view — that chametz is not called permitted absorption since chametz is placed on it, unlike kodshim which is not called notar before its prohibition time, and one must distinguish between large and small; and this even for the first answer regarding a small knife — since its use is not via fire, libun is not required as written in the baraita; and so too Rashba — that in any event for all a knife needs only hagalah, and he deleted from the text of Avodah Zarah 'knives' since in Tosefta it is not found; and Ran and Tosafot; however Rabbenu Yitzchak ben Meir wrote that even a small one requires libun, since sometimes one fixes the wick of fat and turns meat over coals; and Rabbenu Tam rejected his view since its primary use is not via fire, and so too Ran; and proof — that in every vessel we follow the majority of its use, like cups and small jugs — even though sometimes they are used in hot, nevertheless we follow its primary use and rinse them; and Beit Yosef wrote that according to Tosafot's conclusion one must distinguish between that of Pesachim and that of Chullin and Tosefta — between a small one that has no crevices etc.; and the Mechaber's words appear to require study — for Yoreh De'ah siman 121 writes both large and small, and even if it has no crevices, libun is required to cut hot with it; and here he wrote regarding knives in general etc., and afterward wrote in seif 7 regarding vessels etc., such as spits and skewers require libun; and the main point is that he ruled like Rif and Rosh that there is no distinction between chametz and other prohibitions, for otherwise the entire siman would be hidden and libun would not apply at all to chametz; and even though Rabbenu Tam distinguishes between small and large, Yoreh De'ah is concerned to rule like Rabbenu Yitzchak ben Meir stringently in general, for here he ruled like Rabbenu Tam and Ran as written in seif 6: all vessels we follow etc.; and furthermore that even for Rabbenu Yitzchak ben Meir libun is not required except the tip of the knife as Rosh wrote in Avodah Zarah, except stringently he wrote thus; unlike a knife of chametz of a Jew — its manner of use is not via fire even in a large knife, and therefore he wrote here in general:
beur-hagra/3:ב: And kli rishon etc. — Shabbat 42b: the ladle and the pot etc., and there in Gemara he holds etc. that in kli rishon etc. it cooked etc., and he concludes that in kli rishon too it did not cook, and if on the fire — impossible; Ran:
beur-hagra/3:ד: Only. — there that one passes them while boiling, and as written in Yerushalmi chapter 3 of Shabbat and chapter 1 of Maaser, and as explained above:
beur-hagra/3:ו: Therefore. — Rosh in chapter Kol Sha'ah, and we learn also from Yerushalmi end of Avodah Zarah as above, according to Tosafot's explanation there:
beur-hagra/4:א: Seif 4 — and there are those who are lenient. — meaning Mordechai end of Avodah Zarah wrote that those vessels that absorbed permitted do not require libun thus, only if the wood was burned from outside that libun penetrates from side to side and that suffices, since permitted absorption suffices with hagalah as written in our sugya, and that libun is no worse than hagalah and expels more than hagalah; and Beit Yosef wrote per the view of those who say that chametz, since its name of prohibition was placed on it, absorbs prohibited — also such libun does not suffice and complete libun is required, and so too in Shulchan Aruch, and Darkei Moshe in s.k. 5 wrote, and in Orchot Chayyim wrote that chametz is called permitted absorption as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 121, and this is what is meant by and there are those who are lenient if etc.:
beur-hagra/4:ב: And the practice etc. — this is written according to what Beit Yosef wrote in the name of Hagahot Maimoniyot that the world practiced like the words of those who forbid, that chametz equals other prohibitions:
beur-hagra/4:ד: The coating. — there in Mordechai and Magen Avraham:
beur-hagra/5:ב: If their use etc. — Rif and Rosh in chapter Kol Sha'ah, and we learn from what is written there: a rotten tree — one kasher it in boiling water, and in kli rishon as it absorbs so it expels — 40 specifically, because one uses it in kli rishon; but an item used in kli sheini, kli sheini suffices:
beur-hagra/5:ג: And vessels whose use etc. — as written in Yerushalmi Shabbat and Maaser there, and pouring is like kli rishon — R' Yochanan derived from this: one who cooked in it and one who poured into it etc.:
beur-hagra/5:ד: Rather one requires etc. — as it absorbs so it expels as above, but kli rishon does not suffice; through pouring which does not absorb and expel except to the depth of a peel as written in Pesachim 76a, and therefore he required at the end of Avodah Zarah a large pouring spout, and they did not kasher through pouring; and specifically regarding yayin nesech which is cold they said there 'its heat was cooled' — and as they distinguished regarding small vessels chapter 2 of Avodah Zarah, and in chapter Kol Sha'ah there: its use etc.:
beur-hagra/6:א: Seif 6 — all vessels etc. — as above from that of cups etc.:
beur-hagra/6:ב: And there are those who are stringent etc. and likewise etc. and there are etc. — Tosafot Avodah Zarah there 74b s.v. that he expounded who hold specifically when it is known that they were used only cold, and so too; and in Shabbat 42b s.v. but, and in Zevachim 96a:
beur-hagra/6:ג: And bowls etc. — for the reason of pouring is not like kli rishon because it cools as written in Pesachim 76a 'when it cools for him etc.' unlike here:
beur-hagra/8:א: Seif 8 — one etc. — metal vessels are explicit at the end of Avodah Zarah and explicit in the parashah as written there; and wooden and stone vessels are judged like metal vessels — to exclude the view of Rav Hai who wrote that their law is like pottery vessels and require heating in an oven; and proof from what is written at the end of Avodah Zarah: a stone press etc., and of wood etc., and of pottery etc. — evidently their law is not like pottery vessels; and in chapter 5 of Kelim: an oven, a stone basket, and of metal — pure and impure because of metal vessels; a stove etc.; and see in siman 14, and as Rav Avraham ben Natan wrote that we derive prohibition from impurity as written at the end of Avodah Zarah 75a and Niddah 65, in the manner they said regarding taharot etc.; but in Tosefta Zevachim it is taught: stone vessels do not require emptying and rinsing, rather one rinses them; and they forced Mordechai to say that this 'one rinses them' means one kasher them — forced; and furthermore according to one who says emptying in hot is because of hagalah, as written in Zevachim:
beur-hagra/9:_: Seif 9 — one who kasher etc. — will also be explained in siman 452 seif 1:
beur-hagra/10:_: Seif 10 — baskets. — see above siman 127 that he ruled like the latter view, and all the more so here regarding salting; Magen Avraham — see siman 447 seif 6:
beur-hagra/11:א: Seif 11 — pan. — even though one fries in it as written in Tosefta Avodah Zarah: pots and hot waters and one fries etc. — one rinses them in boiling water:
beur-hagra/11:ב: And there are those who are stringent. — Magen Avraham: sometimes etc., and it is like its use via fire; and Rosh rejected their view — for if so, in a pot too one should be concerned; rather that there is moisture of liquid in the cooked food, only that at the side of the wall it is dry, and it is not called its use via fire:
beur-hagra/12:א: Seif 12 — all vessels. — since we say in chapter Kol Sha'ah: take them in boiling water, and as written there 74a: if part of it is hot, all of it is hot; Rashba:
beur-hagra/12:ב: However if. — Ran rejected his words — for if so, R' Ashi should have said also take them in fire; rather that a knife has two uses — one via fire and that use does not reach the handle, and one in boiling water and it also reaches the handle; and specifically regarding kodshim we say in Zevachim 96b: if one cooked in part of the vessel etc., and as written there: terumah does not require etc.; and so too in Tur Yoreh De'ah and in the gloss siman 121 seif 6; but from Tosafot's words in Zevachim there — that for all prohibitions kashering is required in the entire vessel, see there; and Rashba has the text in Pesachim: bring them in and take them in boiling water, and hagalah at the end he relied on, and iron ones in fire first — stringency in general as poskim wrote and Magen Avraham; and Shulchan Aruch and the Rav follow their approach that Beit Yosef in Yoreh De'ah chapter siman 121 like Rashba — that even if one used only part of it, kashering is required in all of it, and so too in Shulchan Aruch there seif 6; but in the gloss there like Tur's view who disagrees with him because of keved kefel, and even though he explained there siman 94 seif 1 and siman 98 seif 4 in the gloss that we do not say 'if part is hot all is hot' — nevertheless one must say according to keved kefel because he did not rule thus except for this matter that it does not expel from that side, but to absorb he explained in siman 92 seif 5 that it absorbs, and according to Tosafot in Zevachim there — that if all is hot it absorbs in all of it, and there is no distinction between metal vessels except that in metal vessels if all is hot, even if not at the fire on its other part — unlike Shach there siman 121 s.k. 17, and so we hold above siman 94 etc.:
beur-hagra/12:ג: There is no need to forbid etc. — it implies from Taz's words there and the Rav there even if one used on that side that was not kashered — unlike Magen Avraham:
beur-hagra/12:ד: And even etc. — that it is not all hot more than pouring, and such is Darkei Moshe in the name of Orchot Chayyim: l'chatchila it is good to kasher it, for behold they touch it all year with dirty hands; however through pouring even l'chatchila — end of his words; and I saw many who are lenient even l'chatchila, and it is good to kasher it l'chatchila according to Orchot Chayyim, and all this unlike Magen Avraham; and all this when one did not use all of it, but if one used — certainly kashering part of it does not suffice as written above and as written in Zevachim there: if one cooked in part of the vessel etc.; but if one cooked in all of it — certainly kashering part of it does not suffice for all:
beur-hagra/13:א: Seif 13 — vessel etc. if. — since he does not require mention of the handle in chapter Kol Sha'ah; Mordechai:
beur-hagra/13:ג: And if etc. — and therefore they said: no — take them etc., and afterward etc., that libun through plaster which is the handle does not help, and all the more so hagalah; and see in the explanation of Tosefta seif 1:
beur-hagra/14:א: Seif 14 — cover etc. that covers — as written in chapter 2 of Machshirin: an impure bathhouse, its sweat is impure; and a pure one in a householder's pool in the house — etc.; and we derive prohibition from tumah as written above seif 8.
beur-hagra/15:_: Seif 15 — cover — for its use is through fire; see Magen Avraham.
beur-hagra/16:א: Seif 16 — mortar etc. and there are those who are stringent — their dispute depends on what is written in chapter Kol Sha'ah there 'except for a yeast container' etc., and Rashi explained even through hagalah; Arukh and Rabbenu Yonah and all the poskim explained without hagalah — see above siman 452; and likewise for a mortar; and even though Rosh in his rulings wrote that Rashi concedes regarding a mortar at the end of the chapter — he did not write so, and so all the poskim.
beur-hagra/17:א: Seif 17 — the board etc. and likewise — from what is written there 'these troughs of Mechoza' etc., and specifically that kneading is always done in them as written in the Gemara there; and so too Mahar"i Weil and Mordechai; except that Mordechai wrote one should not be lenient after they already practiced custom, because of permitted things that became forbidden through custom.
beur-hagra/18:א: Seif 18 — the sieve — see above siman 442 from what is at the end of Avodah Zarah that linen garments are cleaned — meaning with water and ash; and all the more so regarding something that adheres as written in Zevachim daf 79b and as written above.
beur-hagra/21:א: Seif 21 — barrels etc. permitted through hagalah or etc. — as written regarding yayin nesech in Avodah Zarah daf 33a, halacha lema'aseh, one fills them — etc.; and there daf 75a one who wants to purify them immediately hagels them in boiling water; and they said there daf 34a; and in chapter Kol Sha'ah there is mention of yayin nesech and chametz etc. — there its use etc.; if so, in chametz for something whose use is cold it is equivalent to yayin nesech; and even though hagalah does not help for pottery vessels except when its use is hot, as Rosh wrote in the mishnah there daf 44b regarding ne'ivah artachu in pottery that pouring does not help without peeling — therefore he commanded to hagal them for then peeling is not needed; and as written daf 33a that even pouring helps for pottery; and all the more hagalah as Rosh wrote Shabbat chapter 3 siman 11 that hagalah is better than pouring, for pouring does not help for something whose use is hot even in other vessels; and in Jerusalem Talmud end chapter 2 of Pesachim Rabbi Ami taught regarding cheese baskets, one fills them with water three days from erev Pesach; and all the more hagalah as above; and so Hagahot Oshr"i chapter 2 of Avoda Zara siman 105 s.v. betashmisho etc.
beur-hagra/21:ב: And b'dieved — there in Hagahot Oshr"i and see Magen Avraham in the name of Mordechai; and what Mordechai wrote: since permitted absorbs — etc., meaning as written in chapter 3 siman 477 that we estimate against the whole; and since sometimes it absorbs and sometimes emits one cannot stand on the matter — etc., meaning that even if it is known how much exits from it, nevertheless it returns and absorbs and what was absorbed becomes nevelah and returns and emits — not so in permitted that it becomes nevelah as Tosafot wrote Avodah Zarah daf 76a s.v. bat; but in a vessel of permitted — etc., and Beit Yosef wrote; and it was already explained that for most poskim chametz is not called permitted and therefore they omitted it in Shulchan Aruch; and likewise nitelaf we hold in siman 447 seif 10 that it is forbidden; and Magen Avraham; and see Tehudah siman 201.
beur-hagra/22:ג: Except for a yeast container etc. forbidden — as Rosh's text 'all vessels' etc. and we do not read 'in cold' but it deals with hot.
beur-hagra/22:ד: But forbidden to knead — Taz; and Rosh wrote that it is possible per the text 'use matzah in cold' and because of the end regarding a yeast container that even in cold it is forbidden — such as kneading in them.
beur-hagra/22:ה: And all this etc. — as Arukh's explanation and all the poskim as written above in seif 16.
beur-hagra/22:ו: But for charoset etc. — as written in the Gemara there and as written above in seif 1; and this is according to Tur who disagrees with what is written in seif 21 that for something whose use is cold even in pottery hagalah helps as Tur wrote there; and from Rav Hai Gaon's words it appears hagalah does not help for pottery even if one used it only in cold — etc., see there; but according to what Shulchan Aruch ruled in seif 21 that hagalah helps, and likewise yayin nesech even though it is sharp and very strong — likewise here; and so too in Milchamot explicitly there that a house of yeast and a house of charoset have the law like yayin nesech; see there and in Ran who expanded there.
beur-hagra/22:ח: Even in cold — but Bach and Peri Chadash emended in Tur and wrote that it should read 'only in cold' — to exclude Rosh and Rif and Rambam; Tur wrote pottery is equal in this to other vessels; but their words require study, for if so what is 'and even if one did not use' etc., what is its extension — behold in other vessels too the law is likewise; and above where he wrote 'but in cold' etc. he should have written 'and even pottery' as he began 'all vessels even' etc.
beur-hagra/22:ט: And nowadays etc. — there in Rif; and meaning even other pottery even if one used only in cold — the law of a yeast container of pottery.
beur-hagra/22:כ: And forbidden — meaning actual matzah b'eyna; but in a pot there is no prohibition b'dieved as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 92 seif 8.
beur-hagra/23:א: Seif 23 — fused with glass — as Tosafot explained Avodah Zarah daf 33b s.v. konya, that Rabbenu Tam challenged Rashi's explanation there and in chapter Kol Sha'ah regarding coating a limb — why is it worse than if it were entirely a limb where hagalah helps; and so Mordechai in chapter Kol Sha'ah; and they further challenged there that konya does not imply a limb as written in Zevachim siman 60 s.v. vikonya; see there in Tosafot Avodah Zarah; and Rambam and Tur explained like Rashi; and so Tosafot explained Avodah Zarah daf 75b s.v. vehalakhta; and so there in Shulchan Aruch Yoreh De'ah siman 120 seif 1 and there in siman 135 seif 6 he wrote both explanations; and see Tosafot Ketubot daf 107b s.v. hani etc.
beur-hagra/23:ב: And there are places — Magen Avraham and Taz.
beur-hagra/24:_: Seif 24 — and there are places that are stringent — Magen Avraham s.k. 47; and see Gemara Avodah Zarah daf 74b Rava etc.
beur-hagra/25:ד: Whether they are of wood etc. — the above baraita deals with metal; and of wood their law is like metal as written above in seif 8.
beur-hagra/25:ז: However etc. — as above seif 6 in the gloss; and so in Mordechai siman 464 because sometimes they boil in them etc.
beur-hagra/26:א: Seif 26 — glass vessels even etc. — for in such a case kashering is required even in cold as written in Avodah Zarah daf 33a and daf 74b; and even though poskim disagree there whether it deals with pottery specifically or even other vessels — nevertheless for pottery it is not so, and glass vessels are like pottery as written below; nevertheless kashering is not required for they do not absorb as written in Pesachim daf 74b that the heart of a date palm is different; and see Rashi Shabbat daf 15b s.v. bekli zekhukhit etc.; and Yoreh De'ah siman 135 seif 8; and therefore even if one used in hot kashering is not required as Lev wrote there; and explicitly it is taught in Avot derabbi Nathan chapter 41: pottery absorbs and does not emit — etc.; glass does not absorb and does not emit — etc.; in a warm place warm, in a cold place cold; and even though it was asked regarding konya of date palm whether it absorbed — we see it applies there because it is a small coating; but a whole glass vessel does not absorb; Tosafot Avodah Zarah there s.v. hanal konya etc.; see there.
beur-hagra/26:ג: There is no etc. — since it was asked regarding konya and likewise yayin nesech; and Yoreh De'ah siman 135 seif 8; and see Ran chapter 2 in the sugya there.
beur-hagra/26:ד: And there are those who are stringent — because it is like a pottery vessel since the beginning of their creation is from sand as written in chapter 1 of Shabbat; and so we hold in the conclusion in the words of Rav Ashi; and even though its use is in cold, nevertheless sometimes they use them in hot and soak bread crumbs from erev Pesach in them like cooked; Mordechai in siman 465; and as written in seif 25 in the gloss that we are concerned even for use that is not fixed as above; and therefore even hagalah does not help for them like pottery as written in Avodah Zarah there and in chapter Kol Sha'ah there 'and the Torah testified regarding pottery' etc.; Tehudah; and so it is taught explicitly in Avot derabbi Nathan that it does not emit like a pottery vessel; and what is written there that it does not absorb — meaning like pottery in the beginning that absorbs even in cold immediately even if one does not put it away for permanent use as written in Avodah Zarah daf 33b keshai etc.; and proof from what is written 'and does not emit'; and what is written regarding the heart of a date palm does not stand in the conclusion there as Tosafot wrote there s.v. she'ani; and so it appears in Tosafot Avodah Zarah above that hagalah does not help — for they challenged Rashi who explained regarding a limb that if so why does hagalah not help; and they explained regarding glass only that he wrote an entirely glass vessel does not absorb as above.
peri-megadim/1:_: And good [Taz]. Bach forbids placing in great height both chametz vessels on Pesach and Pesach vessels the rest of the year — they are collateral vessels from the reason of lest one forget. But Pesach vessels in great height is a remote concern lest one forget and use chametz; and on Pesach lest one use matzah — but even if so, we hold nitelaf is permitted on Pesach, as in siman 447. Rosh forbids all year and Magen Avraham forbids even without a partition. Bach was stringent even above a place a person's hand does not reach; Magen Avraham upheld the custom; the Acharonim agreed. Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote that one may permit with a partition similar to burying — see Rokeach on siman 447 note 4. Or one may say paytanim mean: even pottery that has no remedy except breaking — nevertheless they permitted on Pesach with sufficient partitions to bury them similar; and it requires study in the explanations of their piyyutim. Maaseh Rokeach wrote not to leave year-round without a partition — we are also concerned thus even in vessels that are not ben yomo, since we are strict even for a minute amount of chametz; and per what we hold in the Rav's gloss on siman 447 to forbid even in any amount and nitelaf on Pesach. And it is good to lock them in a room — such is Tur's language from Rosh responsum general rule 14 siman 1 — not like Beit Yosef; Bach quarreled with those who place tin chametz vessels above an unreachable place; Minchat Yehudah disagreed; such is practiced. "Not any pottery vessel used hot" — Beit Yosef explained: even if one did not use it except in kli sheini — heating does not help; Rambam equates pottery kli sheini to kli rishon. The Mechaber appears to have copied Tur's language — his intent to forbid even in kli sheini, like the Rama's view in the gloss; but Rabbeinu Moshe in Darkei Moshe wrote per Tur it does not absorb except through kli rishon or via pouring — not like Beit Yosef. The Mechaber's own view too is that it absorbs and becomes forbidden; explicit from seif 5: and if their use is in kli sheini — kasher them in kli sheini. For the law, one who examines Rif, Rambam, Rosh and poskim — it is not explained that the vessel is forbidden through kli sheini; only in bowls whose use is via pouring. Nevertheless in a case of great loss — especially in a vessel that is not ben yomo — it appears to me to be lenient b'dieved if one used a vessel used in kli sheini, even pottery, since the majority of Rishonim agreed kli sheini does not absorb; nat bar nat for detriment — many are lenient regarding chametz. Lest one be concerned lest they crack — since they were fired all year from outside — not so with ovens fired from inside; Minchat Yehudah general rule 60 note 2; not like Bach; see siman 461. Forbidden to use it even cold in a fixed manner — Minchat Yehudah general rule 11 note 16; not like Olat Shabbat; fixed manner — even orally after its prohibition time; Taz agrees; not like Peri Chadash Yoreh De'ah siman 98; see Solut leMinchah.
peri-megadim/2:א: But [Taz] the Rosh wrote for the Mechaber in seif 2 and so in Tur, and he corrected in this because he said there specifically if one heated inside — but in a kiln whose flame is from every side it is not extinguished; how did he say in our ovens it is not extinguished, since the flame is from every side it is not extinguished? See Perishah therefore Taz explained: even in a kiln too, if one waits a long time sometimes it is extinguished; but in a short time it whitens well, and in a short time it is not extinguished — the flame rises from every side — unlike an oven that requires waiting inside and sealing and removing immediately lest it be extinguished. And if so the explanation is: since one inserts for great heating such as this, certainly he does not seal lest it be extinguished — for in a short time certainly it is not extinguished from every side, and a short time suffices; but Bach explained: since one inserts for great heating — if it is extinguished, it is extinguished immediately and he abandons it — see Magen Avraham note 4; and see there.
peri-megadim/2:ב: And if he gave heat in the oven and it became white so that sparks fly and he passed and cooked on Pesach intentionally — forbidden, since it is like cooking in a vessel ab initio forbidden; in shogeg it appears permitted. And if a noksha fell like crust in siman 462 seif 2 for a pot — hagalah does not help; it appears to me siman 113 seif 6 in Shulchan Aruch — he kashered it via fire because the essence is not in the noksha — it appears the essence is in the noksha, a fence against full chametz; or since they say noksha of dough — then the essence is in the noksha. And if there were permission even in Peri Chadash for Magen Avraham siman 462 note 5 — except we do not have it; as stated.
peri-megadim/4:א: And if [Taz] Magen Avraham note 4 — burned bricks — libun specifically; and brick dried in the sun has the law of an earthenware vessel (and is permitted through hagalah); but if they heated it outside — even b'dieved forbidden as its use — kasher it as they swallow chametz inside even though they always heat outside; so in the Gemara and Levush; Boukia — they heated outside and forbidden in it; and metal vessels specifically — one fills coals inside; outside even if use is always thus and it whitens until sparks fly — forbidden b'dieved; so in Tur; see below seif and the same for metals that one kasher through hagalah if one inserts into a yorah until its rim and afterward that portion and the water did not enter inside — even b'dieved forbidden.
peri-megadim/4:ב: If they heated beer hot on pottery vessels outside that absorbed like k deposit and returned to our oven — even if we say per the Gemara's meaning Pesachim 4b that such is not impure like k deposit — Magen Avraham note 3 and see there; nevertheless it requires study b'dieved intentionally whether to forbid the cooked food on Pesach; l'chatchila the Rashba already wrote note 3 in the name of Ohr Zaru'a that they are not accustomed even to return to kilns; however b'dieved or in time of pressure one may be lenient via kilns if he has no other vessels.
peri-megadim/5:א: Knives [Taz] Pesachim 4b — and it appears in other issurim hagalah suffices even though sometimes they roast on a knife on fire — they follow the majority of their use; nitelaf such as this is permitted — unlike Pesach where they asked whether nitelaf is permitted or forbidden — he said for his view he was stringent new like BY siman 447 seif and below seif 6; see there. And in the piyyut "knives for meals" for a meal; and Magen Avraham wrote seif 5 note 5 — where possible to be concerned — there is no remedy even where impossible; and so all that have grooves in the blade — there is no remedy in hagalah; and b'dieved even if one kashered a vessel that has a groove and it is impossible to scrape — Acharonim note 16 — even b'dieved forbidden without libun — not like Bach; and so the halacha; and the reason: all vessels that have protrusions and rims and cracks or old pewter like talya'ir taken from gentiles and they are cut in the knife — many splits and it is impossible to scrape the grooves well without rust remaining — truly no remedy in hagalah. And a knife whose cauldron cannot be cleaned and hagalah and cutting food in the flame — not forbidden; see EH 121 seif 6.
peri-megadim/5:ב: Nachmanides wrote note 1 — a knife of metal: the blade and the cauldron and they used also in the cauldron in boiling water, and afterward inserted the cauldron in wood — hagalah does not help; this is true and established like Talui in seif 13 and Levush; and b'dieved if one inserts in the flame on Pesach via hagalah — it requires study; Magen Avraham note 24 — metal hot in part is not hot in whole to emit from side of the blade even if used in whole first in boiling water; and in Yoreh De'ah 121 in Shach note 16 — it does not appear so — for he used first at the fire itself and now used in the flame at the fire itself; even though afterward he libuned the blade and cauldron was in tin — he has no way to permit; see there note 15; and see Magen Avraham seif 4; see note 13 regarding knives in a horn and similarly; see note 6 regarding laws of immersing vessels in knives and similarly.
peri-megadim/5:ג: Or one may say Rabbina said to Rav Ashi — specifically a Pesach knife, for in a simple issur libun; and from meat to milk hagalah — only Pesach whether it is called permitted absorption or forbidden absorption; see note 8; and see Tosafot Pesachim 30b s.v. vehalakhta.
peri-megadim/5:ד: And know Rashi — even when removed from fire as the Mechaber wrote, and proof from Alfas that they passed through boiling water — meaning for a knife whose main use is in hot bread removed from fire, and the piece placed in talya'ir — Peri Megadim holds we do not follow the majority of use; one must insert on the fire and water raises boiling like Beit Yosef siman 462 seif 1; see Magen Avraham note 6 and note 7. And indeed a thing absorbed via fire requires libun — all that was removed from fire then has no law of libun; therefore Magen Avraham wrote note 6 to insert in a pan while still hot; Mahari Weil in the first chapter — a table requires hagalah specifically; see Magen Avraham note 37; see note 92 seif 7 in the gloss — they placed a hot pot on spilled milk in cold — the pot is forbidden and the food permitted — it requires study from Alfas that passed through boiling water — it implies even if he left in a cold place; and also Peri Megadim holds a lump forbids all the more — it requires study that law; and therefore those knives with which they cut hot bread removed from fire — hagalah suffices while still in the oven even if scraped and sealed; the oven is called via fire; see Magen Avraham note 21 from this. And Peri Chadash note 14 wrote additionally that knives have another leniency — namely a small knife.
peri-megadim/6:א: All [Taz] the Rosh in Pesachim 4b and Bach and Levush — rust does not interrupt and he relied on a verse kli rishon from Yoreh De'ah. It appears like Talui in seif 13 — rust interrupts kli rishon; and therefore if one removed rust and cleaned well and did not use it further and rust returned — nevertheless one must again remove rust and libun; Taz implies hagalah helps for him because hagalah water acts within rust and rust particles — only the reason is because of adhesion in the eye where it does not help; therefore since the reason is from the eye — if there are grooves in a knife that cannot be cleaned in the eye even without rust etc. — and from this support for his words; and in a black rust that removed in the eye — no concern d'alma; however libun in place of rust alone suffices and one must more as in note 7 and in the gloss seif 5 and Peri Chadash note 9; and it is simple that if one wants to whiten thus he is permitted — only it deals with one who wanted to remove and cannot — then his advice is to libun. And therefore Levush relied on it — only immersion lest there be an interposition; see EH 121 seif 13; and it is reasonable hagalah does not act in the eye. (At present they smear from bricks not raw and not finished — finished like stones are pure and require sprinkling and finished ones are impure — it requires study presently).
peri-megadim/6:ב: And regarding immersion — see EH 121 seif 13 — one must remove rust even in new vessels that the gentile never used at all. Minor rust that is not significant is permitted. And behold Stofel the advisor and Radalakh for Taz — immersion without a blessing; and Shach requires immersion — there note 127 note 7 and note 11. In Lublin they place matzot on them even for Shach — immersion because it is fit for food use — pepper mill immersion with a blessing seif 67; and mill of Kaufbeuren for Shach — immersion without blessing because it requires cooking — R' Eizen who makes all the vessels for gentiles — immersion with a blessing because they crumble bread; and R' Eizen who buys from gentiles in Lublin and pierces and vessels of measures in this manner — it requires study; see EH 121 seif 10 in the gloss and in Bach — a Jew acquired metal vessels from gentiles and made a vessel — no immersion needed like in Yoreh De'ah there — there is no gentile name on it at all initially — plate; and now a vessel — unlike Lublin only a Jew pierces and makes a measure — it appears immersion without blessing; and it is simple to me if a Jew acquired in Lublin from gentiles and attached thus for talya'ir and similarly — requires immersion and even with blessing is possible since the gentile name did not change. A griddle that gentiles coated with pewter — the Rosh z"l siman 43 requires immersion; Peri Chadash disputes; there they wrote in manuscript to immerse without a blessing.
peri-megadim/6:ג: A minor has no credibility — see EH 121 Taz note 14 — metal vessels of Torah; and in siman 462 I wrote it requires study whether even glass which is d'rabbanan like BY siman 137 seif 3 in the gloss — presumption of issur Magen Avraham note 8. However in glass — all that reached libun must check afterward; and metals — it appears one must know it is large; see siman 199 Magen Avraham note 7 and Peri To'eh note 7 — it requires study. And laws of immersing vessels are many; see in Tosefta; I will explain further. See end of Megillah language "scoured and rinsed in water".
peri-megadim/7:_: And one needs [Taz] and Peri Chadash here l'chatchila to scrape them even with libun per Rashba's view Yoreh De'ah 121; see Magen Avraham; and see there.
peri-megadim/8:_: Such as [Taz]. I did not merit to understand his holy words on Bene from siman 462 seif 4 — it does not return and become stirred even after six until the night — forbidden; however it is nullified in sixty and does not return and become stirred. And if from what is written in note 5 that one can add — since still permitted — apparently permitted absorption is hard; whence do we know this? And first one can say it is difficult for him that he holds a spit — meaning they roast meat from salted meat that was not checked — and it is difficult since already nullified in sixty before Pesach; if so for something — hagalah suffices l'chatchila as in seif 27 in the spit — also this requires study whence this — say l'chatchila requires libun even for something in the spit. And if heating the spit is like hagalah — if so why permitted in seif 27 where chametz did not touch the spit itself and we do not nullify absorption in a vessel as Magen Avraham wrote note 4 and Peri To'eh; if so the reason is they were nullified before Pesach; and he searched the house end of the siman; Magen Avraham note 51. And it is possible his intent here deals with a spit that roasted chametz b'eyna; it deals that if in unsalted meat not checked on the spit — he holds the Mechaber was not stringent to libun for this because it is something even l'chatchila not to roast on this spit like seif 27 — that it returns and becomes stirred as Levush's meaning (though the cooked food is permitted but to roast l'chatchila afterward — no); nevertheless something absorbed via the fat of the meat is like a griddle in seif 1 — since there is a small amount of oil — here too via fat — hagalah suffices; and therefore he explained it deals with chametz b'eyna; and griddle the reason there is a small amount of oil — permitted in hagalah Magen Avraham notes 21 and 22; and Magen Avraham wrote in Mordechai — permitted absorption there are other reasons; Peri Chadash note 22 and so. And Magen Avraham wrote on the Rambam note 11 in the name of Ohr Zaru'a; and the Rambam and custom — Taz certainly there is no dispute and all agree that a thing requiring hagalah — in libun is lenient; and a thing requiring libun requires sparks (or one removes the upper peel Taz note 24) — it requires study if light libun burns in the eye and one must remove rust; or when there is rust requires libun with sparks such as this; see note 7 and the world places only coals in place of rust — it requires study.
peri-megadim/9:א: Rather [Taz] the general rule: as its use so kasher it — if used via pouring requires pouring without interruption of the stream; if used in kli rishon on fire requires that one kasher in a large yorah and raises boiling specifically like BY siman 462 note 3; and if used in kli rishon after removed from fire — b'dieved in this that one places into such a kli rishon; Peri Chadash; and l'chatchila they practice all in a yorah on fire and raises boiling and bubbles; Levush wrote pouring requires also a second time — they wondered at Peri Megadim; and I say that in pouring from kli rishon without interruption of the stream — once; and so is the halacha; and perhaps it is a mistake there.
peri-megadim/9:ב: And know that the general rule: as their use so kasher them; and as the Mechaber decided — all the more so in kli sheini and in Bach seif 8 he brought in the name of Rabbeinu Shmuel Mitzulani that ShTat holds in kli sheini hagalah does not help — only kli rishon; and Peri Chadash in seif 5 wrote — whence does he have this; and Ramah in Peri Chadash the Great and Berach in Responsa — it appears kli sheini requires pouring; Magen Avraham note 3 and Rash STat holds pouring is a doubt whether like kli rishon and we require kli rishon — it requires study. And indeed kli sheini and kli shelishi — their absorption and emission are not equal. And also talya'ir on which they place a lump — for one who is stringent see note 94; Magen Avraham siman 462 note 15 — hagalah via pouring also does not help because water cools; and a lump in kli sheini its law is like kli rishon and requires hagalah from the law that it should be kli rishon.
peri-megadim/9:ג: Pickled from time to time — forbidden in a vessel or chametz beer for one who forbids because it absorbs and emits in whole; and even in metal vessels; and as we must say below at end of the siman — see there; nevertheless if one kashered in kli rishon removed from fire — b'dieved in this even though it does not raise boiling; see note 61; and Peri Chadash in Shach note 127 — but via pouring — forbidden even b'dieved because pouring is a doubt whether it cooks like a peel or not; and to be stringent not to be lenient — therefore even a vessel forbidden via salting from chametz — which does not absorb in a vessel except like k deposit — hagalah via pouring does not help; see in Peri Megadim Yoreh De'ah 98. And nevertheless this doubt of pouring — one does not make from it a doubt to be lenient unless if a doubt whether pouring forbids in it and similarly; and to say perhaps not pouring and perhaps it does not cook and does not absorb at all — no. And proof from Yoreh De'ah siman 98 and 92 — and pouring in blood forbids; and blood that cooked in it is d'rabbanan — apparently it is not a doubt. And also without this it is clear from many places thus.
peri-megadim/9:ד: If a vessel absorbed issur via pouring and one kashered in kli sheini and cooked in it the food — permitted without great loss — why should we be concerned for it? If per Taz Yoreh De'ah 105 note 4 Derush — it appears without the blade in kli sheini that absorbs — behold it was kashered in kli sheini; and if from the reason of pouring — pouring cooks only like a peel and there are sixty in the food against the peel of the vessel alone — in a wide bowl — see Yoreh De'ah 92 seif 2 note 4 unlike Pesach without the blade — there is to forbid Magen Avraham siman 462 note 127; and so is the halacha; and even with the blade — there is to forbid — it requires study.
peri-megadim/9:ה: See Yoreh De'ah 92 Taz note 34 — if one inserts a vessel into a yorah on the fire and raises boiling and removes the vessel from there — one does not kasher from this vessel onto a kli rishon — meaning if used in kli rishon removed from fire and absorbed chametz — b'dieved hagalah in kli rishon even though it does not raise boiling; or a vessel via pickling — kli rishon suffices even though it does not raise boiling; but to draw in a cold vessel from kli rishon — even though it waited inside kli rishon on the fire and raised boiling inside this vessel — when he removed to be stringent — it is not like kli rishon literally that was heated — its sides via fire literally.
peri-megadim/9:ו: If they poured beer strong in one's mouth via pouring to a bowl — it appears its law is like kli rishon as Shach wrote Yoreh De'ah 69 note 38 in the name of Afikei Ravivim — hot kli sheini and sharp absorbs and cooks in whole; and therefore bowls require hagalah in kli rishon literally as stated — for sometimes they pour on them in one's mouth; Magen Avraham siman 462 note 4; and see at end of the siman I will explain further.
peri-megadim/11:א: To kasher [Taz] — it appears a general stringency; and Rashba note 18 — b'dieved one relies on one immersion; Peri Chadash was stringent; and in the name of Ramah Mefanso z"l — if used inside a cover in kli rishon or via fire requires libun; and in my view there are those who are lenient; see there likewise. And bowls — kli rishon suffices even sometimes; they are stringent on the griddle; and in seif 1 there are those stringent on the griddle; and such is the custom; nevertheless all this they are not stringent on bowls matching bowls; Magen Avraham to the Mechaber; see there; and it appears the absorption in them — once from kli rishon or via fire — where did it go? In truth the Mechaber in siman 462 seif 1 — nitelaf on Pesach permitted — they follow majority of use; and once more ab initio and so like an auto kadira in seif 2 that they follow majority of use; and also this is difficult — nitelaf b'dieved permitted not l'chatchila; see in metal vessels from Yoreh De'ah — the Torah did not forbid except in kli rishon; and per the Mechaber we do not nullify d'oraisa issur — behold nitelaf from reason of nullification and only b'dieved permitted; it appears in many ways; but for the Rambam who is stringent in siman 462 nitelaf and something — and even b'dieved they forbid the food and even with the blade — and so is practiced masters of rulings (except to sell if there is to side as in Taz in Magen Avraham note 12) — therefore it is fit to kasher bowls from the law in kli rishon at least; and b'dieved — it requires study. And drinking vessels — the Rambam b'dieved through rinsing because it is not common and we are not concerned perhaps in hot water; and since the Rambam did not emend bowls b'dieved via pouring — it implies one must be stringent. And I saw there are ovens in bowls of tin — cakes in scraped oven and they kasher on Pesach — I said there is no remedy — requires libun; and tin melts — they said it is a new thing; and it is explicit in Magen Avraham note 21 — and what difference to me bowls or bowls; and if you say bowls they bake constantly and bowls majority use pouring — nevertheless l'chatchila and certainly b'dieved; and indeed scraped oven its use is via fire; see Magen Avraham there. And if this bowl became mixed with others — it appears it is not d'shuleim because impossible to libun it is nullified; and in siman 462 Magen Avraham note 40 we wrote from this.
peri-megadim/11:ב: Further there is to investigate — for they place on bowls kreplech and similarly from kli rishon; and also on talya'ir; and Peri Chadash in a lump there are those stringent; and if so even talya'ir requires hagalah in kli rishon specifically; and nevertheless even though it does not raise boiling and was removed from fire — unlike a bowl that sometimes is on the fire — they require on the fire and raises boiling.
peri-megadim/12:_: And one passes [Taz] and Magen Avraham note 18 — it is not like kli rishon literally — a whitened stone; and Peri Chadash note 7 and note 22; see Magen Avraham in this from the law of the stone.
