peri-megadim/13:_: Spoons [Taz] and in Tamim De'im siman 35 — one who is not concerned can kasher; and the halacha is not so; like pottery vessels seif 1 for an oven — it does not help; and so he wrote; and b'dieved if one kashered a forbidden thing and used it intentionally — it requires study — it is like using intentionally in a pot ab initio forbidden; and we do not nullify d'rabbanan issur; see in Peri Megadim Yoreh De'ah. Peri Megadim Eshel Avraham — it is difficult and permitted to kasher — I say in the name of Mahari Weil in Rashba note 23; and Magen Avraham wrote horn spoons etc.; and in Bach seif 8 in the gloss — bone vessels require hagalah and it implies they are permitted because they are hard; see such as this — horn is concerned and bone is hard.
peri-megadim/14:_: Before [Taz] and there in Taz and in Magen Avraham note 1 — see there from many reasons permitted; behold nat bar nat alone — some say chametz is its name on it — see there.
peri-megadim/15:_: Baskets [Taz] — hagalah does not help and one must buy new ones; see seif 18 in vessels — certainly if used chametz hagalah does not help; and there if one left a hot thing — possible even b'dieved forbidden because presumably there is chametz something in the holes; see there; and here in a doubt l'chatchila one must buy new ones; and b'dieved even without hagalah if one salted in twos — one does not forbid from a doubt to establish perhaps there is chametz there; Magen Avraham note 20; and if one salted and chametz something was found in the holes — siman 462 seif 14 and there; and Peri Chadash note 37. And in truth also Taz's intent l'chatchila in a doubt one must be stringent and buy new ones; and b'dieved permitted — unlike baskets below where even b'dieved — it requires study.
peri-megadim/16:א: Griddle [Taz] and Magen Avraham note 1 — chametz is called issur absorption like seif 4 in Taz note 8; and Magen Avraham note 11 — for this matter chametz is called issur absorption and a griddle is permitted because there is fat and it is like water; it appears not to smear with fat — they smear with fat and smearing is slight as Rashba wrote in Tevu'ot Shor 125 note 1 — unlike a griddle even though it dried still much fat remains; see Olas Shabbat note 4 brought; and all the more pots and bowls they smear slightly and it dried completely — requires libun Magen Avraham note 21.
peri-megadim/16:ב: The author said: I have here thoughts of matters and I am setting them forth with God's help. It is simple to me via fire — meaning without intermediaries; but via intermediaries — whether water or other liquids oil and similarly — hagalah helps Magen Avraham note 21; and Shach wrote Yoreh De'ah 121 note 8 in the name of Ramah Mefanso z"l — he distinguished between a griddle of gentiles whose main use is via oil and of Israel via water — meaning oil burns and dries and it is via fire unlike water and they follow majority of use; Peri Chadash here. And behold if gentile roasted nevelah meat in a pot — it requires study — it appears requires libun because before emitting fat it absorbed from the body; and also if they melted fat in a yorah requires libun; and Bach wrote they did not distinguish between a yorah in which they melt fat — it appears in the first chapter thus — in truth in a griddle the reason there is oil unlike milk without intermediaries. Also Shach wrote Yoreh De'ah there from meat to milk requires libun without intermediaries — there is to examine if from milk to meat it is also without intermediaries — though milk is a liquid nevertheless hagalah water does not act except when issur was absorbed via intermediaries — it will be water or other liquids — the body of issur will be water like water poured for gentiles or milk to meat — then hagalah does not act in it; and even per our view chanan and the water became body of issur — the forbidden does not exceed the forbidding and they were not stringent d'rabbanan so much; and therefore a vessel in which they cooked blood even blood that cooked in it is d'rabbanan — in any case even d'rabbanan requires libun and this without intermediaries; and metal vessels the Torah testified to kasher as Rashi wrote in Parashat Matot — pots in hagalah spit in libun and they were not concerned lest gentile used wine certainly in a pot and wine for a nazir as Tosafot in Pesachim. And in Talmud Bavli "kaderata and ascended to fire" (in Bavli it appears Alfasin) — possibly not one manner — behold in hagalah and behold in libun; and possibly from a doubt they were not concerned for this also fat — I am in doubt whether it is like a liquid or food; Magen Avraham note 21 — what difference to me fat or water; see there. End of matter — I am in doubt if via fire requires libun specifically without any liquid; or with liquid even though the liquid forbids — then hagalah water acts; or specifically all that issur was absorbed b'eyna without intermediaries — it will be water — then hagalah water does not act; as appears from what Shach wrote there in griddle milk requires libun and to say butter this is forced; also if so fat certainly in triefah fat and all the more milk triefah and of gentiles such as if they cooked in a pot — do we say requires libun in metals and hagalah does not suffice — it requires study greatly.
peri-megadim/16:ג: Again I saw it implies all that absorbed water or other liquids even though they are the body of issur — permitted in hagalah; and siman 462 in hagalah in other liquids and milk and fat — it appears its use is via fire; and Peri Chadash in Shach note 8 — specifically griddle milk fried in butter and cheese requires libun etc.; and even Rav Ashi heated in Avodah Zarah 76a — permitted absorption — in hagalah as Ran wrote brought Peri Chadash Yoreh De'ah note 4 — remainder initially meat and now remainder unlike chametz that its name is on it; and the same meat in milk its name is on it — it did not change (though nat bar nat helps in Bach there another reason that there is no power to connect afterward) — initially meat and now meat.
peri-megadim/16:ד: And one can see — permitted absorption is like it leaned on it; and since it absorbed via fire hagalah water does not act in it — what difference to me permitted and forbidden; and so we challenged nat bar nat; and there is a note; and to say absorption via fire hagalah emits and something remains in it — therefore when permitted absorption entered in it so much; see Peri Chadash note 99 seif 6 in Shach and Taz note 15 and note 23 and note 122 seif 5; and therefore in hot food from the law forbidden something forbids; and in a vessel l"sh nullification Magen Avraham note 21; and therefore until the night if one used in a vessel that requires libun via hagalah — it appears b'dieved permitted because something is nullified in sixty; and indeed this is an error — certainly even b'dieved forbids if one used in a vessel that requires libun via hagalah and cooked in it — it emits bit by bit; l"sh from a half as Magen Avraham wrote in Tur there note 51 — it requires study. And siman 462 note 65 explicit — from meat to milk permitted absorption is called and light libun suffices as Magen Avraham hinted note 11; and Peri Chadash Yoreh De'ah 121 note 8; and see Magen Avraham there further in this.
peri-megadim/17:א: It requires study [Taz] for me his holy words in Yoreh De'ah 121 seif 6 (Taz 128) — Taz explained note 7 what Magen Avraham wrote here — all handles require kashering because absorption travels in whole and does not emit in whole. And so Shach there note 18 — he was astonished what Bach challenged here seif 1 — the words of Tur contradict — l'chatchila requires kashering even the handles — see there; and therefore for whom is it difficult — for the Rambam who permits b'dieved; and the Mechaber there was stringent even b'dieved because absorption travels in whole and does not emit in whole while hot in part also there for the halacha Taz was stringent like the Mechaber and like Rashba z"l — in metal vessels if hot in part absorption travels in whole and to kasher it does not emit in whole and even b'dieved there is to forbid — see there. And it must be said there Taz returned from what Magen Avraham wrote here and here — he holds Tur even l'chatchila holds it suffices to kasher in part like kli rishon; and here l'chatchila requires hagalah all handles of vessels even wood lest boiling chametz spilled on them — therefore pouring like kli rishon suffices. And nevertheless there it implies he holds the Rambam permits l'chatchila to kasher its part — this is wondrous why he was lenient; but b'dieved he agrees that b'dieved kashering its part in metal vessels if he did not use in whole like kli rishon; see Magen Avraham note 24; and in knives he was stringent b'dieved if he did not kasher the cauldron — explicit in seif 3 and Pesachim 4b — both the blade and cauldron in boiling water and even the cauldron of wood and inserted in iron of the blade — nevertheless requires hagalah of the cauldron; and in wood certainly hot in part and not hot in whole because its use is constant and touches many times hot chametz in bread and similarly — therefore even b'dieved if he did not kasher the cauldron and touched on Pesach — forbidden unlike other handles — one does not forbid in a doubt lest chametz spilled on them. And nevertheless if a doubt touched now the cauldron in meat or not — it appears nitelaf on Pesach is a stringency and a d'rabbanan doubt to be lenient; see note 171 in Shach note 3; and in Peri Chadash regarding inserting a spoon; and nevertheless there is to side here in a doubt.
peri-megadim/17:ב: And behold for Rashba z"l there in 121 — in metal vessels hot in part is hot in whole and absorption travels in whole and does not emit in whole; and that which was glued in tin and metal inserted in the cauldron — Taz brought Yoreh De'ah 121 note 7 — it became stuck via libun of the blade and afterward hagalah of the cauldron acts from side to side even the metal inside the cauldron — see there.
peri-megadim/17:ג: And if a knife and iron cauldron and he kashered the blade and not the cauldron and touched on Pesach in the blade while hot — and he knows it did not touch the cauldron at all — it appears there is not to forbid as in Peri Chadash seif 1 and seif 5 and Maharam Mintz z"l that Shach brought in 121 note 15 — see there. And possible chametz in something — it requires study.
peri-megadim/17:ד: It turns out three measures in a knife. (1) A knife whose blade and cauldron are metal — if its use is in hot foods — kasher in hot foods; if use is via fire like bread and pan (Magen Avraham note 6) — libun; and if he kashered the blade and not the cauldron and afterward touched the cauldron in permitted hot food — according to all forbidden because even the Rambam said thus Yoreh De'ah 121 seif 6 if used in whole; and a knife is known as Taz and Rashba note 26; Peri Chadash note 40; and per Magen Avraham and we know that afterward touched in permitted food in the cauldron. And greater — if afterward inserted the knife in wood and kashered thus and afterward removed the wood and touched in cooked food in permitted — forbids even in roasting similar to Talui in seif 12 — but touched with the wood in roasting hot — does not forbid as Shach wrote Yoreh De'ah 105 notes 22 and 23 — from an absorbing vessel emerges without gravy only like a peel and wood interrupts; but inserted in gravy with the wood — forbids because the metal inside the wood was not kashered like Talui. (2) A knife of permitted that touched in the blade issur hot for gravy — l'chatchila fit to kasher all of it; and b'dieved if he did not kasher at all and inserted the cauldron in permitted — not forbidden like that in Peri Chadash seif 1 — one need not estimate except what was inserted even in metal because absorption does not travel in whole as Shach wrote there note 3; and the same does not emit in whole. And even if one would say in permitted certainly against what was inserted — impossible to limit only a bit more — then it is nat bar nat from place to place in a vessel it is simple it is nat bar nat and nat bar nat and the lump; nevertheless in Peri Chadash seif 4 even a forbidden spoon we hold thus; and Magen Avraham note 24 implies if inserted that part that was not kashered — forbids — this appears in issur unlike in kli rishon permitted absorption and from place to place is more than nat bar nat — l'chatchila absorbed in one place and afterward to place of the blade and still permitted; and it appears it spreads in the blade and this and that; and see there further.
peri-megadim/17:ה: The third in a knife that cut meat even on talya'ir except for a lump — it appears forced forbids in kli rishon Taz note 14 Peri Chadash note 14; and all the more one who is stringent there a lump without being forced; and there is not to extend here; see Magen Avraham I will explain further. And Peri Chadash note 14 note 28 — from the presumption the way is to cut in all the blade except the cauldron on the blade — here in this.
peri-megadim/17:ו: I will copy what Magen Avraham wrote in Peri Megadim Yoreh De'ah 121 in Shach note 16 in manuscript — it is difficult to me Rashba z"l that hot in part is hot in whole in metal to absorb not to emit even though he used only in part; and as proven from the knife of Pesach brought in Bach there — if so Rav Ukva on Avodah Zarah 76a note 1 — gadnafa — what it absorbs in sparks Rashi there — behold it absorbs via fire hot in part hot in whole and emits via sparks; and though from meat to milk it appears the lump; or literally nat bar nat — there it deals with one who buys from gentiles; and it appears for the knife of Pesach.
peri-megadim/18:א: For it absorbs [Taz] — behold in Talui there are four concerns. (1) Even if made new — way to soften little by little and enters in the eye beneath it and cannot clean and hagalah does not help for adhesion in the eye. (2) Perhaps before placing the talui there was chametz in the eye; and therefore when cleaned and all the more new — no concern. (3) They do not say such as kli rishon — for when used not in this way it was used; and now talui interrupts when made old. (4) And in note 23 Peri Chadash challenged on this — it appears similar to a vessel used via fire and kashered and used in boiling water — we do not say from a half it emits bit by bit — the same here; and if one would say between them hagalah emits even thick how much — as appears from Rashba's responsum — behold Boukia heated outside and does not help etc.; and a vessel that one inserts into a yorah until its rim and water did not enter inside — simple forbidden — the same here. And see Rosh Pesachim 30b and responsum general rule 14 — it implies thus it emits bit by bit; and Peri Chadash note 8 — hagalah does not help (see there fat in hot water nat bar nat for benefit and proof from gentile's spoon and Peri Chadash note 14 note 11 and there we wrote in manuscript) and so in Tur — concerned to absorb not in the eye; and Magen Avraham wrote that there was a mitzvah to whiten the talui — meaning old talui absorbed from chametz — libun or hagalah as its use kasher it; and not enough that one kasher the talui afterward with the vessel on the eve from this concern; understand; and Bach brought Rashba's words in responsum siman 471; and there is to explain talui new; and so from words of the questioner there place of doubt is place of pressure; and similarly he equated cracks — see there well; and so he answered Rashba z"l — certainly hagalah emits even the vessel very thick all made new — only the concern lest there is in the eye that entered afterward when the talui softened; and therefore even new requires completion and a spoon suffices to burn in the eye the measure beneath the talui (unlike old requires libun of the body of the vessel more in place of talui — understand); and nevertheless note 5 appears he explains before absorption of issur to talui — it requires study; and it appears the concern is because of adhesion in the eye and if so cleaning suffices.
peri-megadim/18:ב: But Mordechai wrote explicitly siman 478 — it implies he holds like kli rishon certainly we say even before absorption of issur to talui from a half; and if cleaned in the eye it is fine when it is strong like a nail and similarly; except here in talui the way is to soften — requires hagalah before fixing the talui — otherwise perhaps at time of hagalah it was attached and hagalah water did not enter beneath the talui; and on Pesach it softened and emits from what was absorbed in the wall opposite the talui — l"sh now from a half; and so Peri Chadash. And Mordechai this that there is to permit from this reason — it is an alternate view — not as Magen Avraham wrote. And therefore Taz challenged — talui new there is concern perhaps it softened and entered in the eye and hagalah cannot help for adhesion in the eye; and missing the word "except" and it must be said this does not deal except when attached very much; and he explains Rashba's words even when made new. And on Tur he challenged — why does it help — perhaps it softened and it is like a crack that there is concern for adhesion in the eye; and it appears it deals with attached strongly; Peri Chadash.
peri-megadim/18:ג: The fourth reason in talui he brought in note 50 and so note 23 — even though they say from a half there is concern perhaps afterward it spreads outside the talui. And for the law — every new l'chatchila one must libun place of talui per Taz; and b'dieved one may be lenient. And in the prior absorption even if cleaned the adhesion — forbidden b'dieved because l"sh like kli rishon and from a half as in the third reason; see 121 Taz note 5. And until the night talui old if there are sixty against place of talui — permitted because the absorbed in the wall is not l"sh; see Peri Chadash note 94. And above in a place without gravy requires sixty times seif 1 slightly less against place of talui Peri Chadash note 24 note 23 and all this when talui inside unlike outside and they do not draw with it from a yorah and similarly — then suffices kashering the talui alone beforehand and not the vessel; and so Peri Chadash; and see Magen Avraham note 27 further.
peri-megadim/19:_: And there is [Taz] what Magen Avraham wrote that one is concerned lest they crack Magen Avraham note 31 in the name of Bach; and see nearby and Magen Avraham; and Magen Avraham wrote from siman 462 per his method there note 13 — sharp residue only nullified in sixty in a mortar that they do not use much; Magen Avraham there note 33; and Magen Avraham wrote in the name of Bach to grind everything before Pesach — it is nat bar nat of permitted Magen Avraham note 31 in sharp l"sh nat bar nat with Bach — some are lenient; and even though we do not hold thus — nevertheless for benefit of the matter they do with hagalah. And one grinds everything before its prohibition time — then one does not nullify issur siman 462 note 5; and Magen Avraham wrote from siman 462 that leaven house from the law that a cow helps. And Rambam wrote light libun suffices because from the law hagalah suffices note 14; and of wood one peels and hagalas afterward because we are concerned for grooves; also some say it is like libun; and even though we do not hold thus — nevertheless what one can do one does. And a vessel of wood that has iron pierced inside like R' Eizen — cannot clean well and there is no remedy in hagalah. And Mechaber wrote whitened stone — this in a mortar that did not absorb via fire; and so in seif 6 in bowls Magen Avraham note 18 — its use is not constant via fire unlike kli rishon that was used at the fire — requires like kli rishon and that they raise boiling at the fire as in Tosefta; and so Peri Chadash here. And Magen Avraham wrote mortars of gentiles are lighter etc. — it appears the reason chametz emits something unlike other issurim; and even though one does not nullify issur l'chatchila see note 99 seif 6 — nevertheless in a mortar of gentiles there is reason to permit because some say hagalah helps unlike chametz they are stringent; likewise a vessel that requires pouring — one does not kasher in kli rishon — note after its prohibition time Tosefta note 1 — because its absorption is slight and it absorbs from other vessels whose absorption is greater. Note 8 — a vessel permitted in hagalah — forbidden to libun it; note copper scrap vessels — concerned lest they crack. And know that even pottery forbidden like k deposit from salting or via pouring — one does not libun in an oven — nevertheless concerned lest they crack even though its absorption is slight; see Magen Avraham; and chametz mortar requires estimating against everything; see note 96 Tznon in a slice and in Peri Megadim there see in the note afterward there.
peri-megadim/21:_: Peel [Taz] — its use is via fire without liquid; and from the law libun; and even though the oven is scraped — it is literally via fire; and so an oven such as this; Magen Avraham note 21. And forbidden to kasher a new winnowing fork for the coming Pesach lest they err etc.; and forbidden even b'dieved a winnowing basket via hagalah; it appears for a mortar in note 19 — there perhaps lest they err b'dieved permitted as in note 19. And a Pesach mixing tub — if they are stringent there is not so much concern because also in mixing chametz permitted from the law in hagalah; see siman 1; and nevertheless why should we do l'chatchila an act unnecessary and they will come to err. And Peri Chadash note 39 he was lenient b'dieved if they kashered a winnowing basket of chametz and removed matzah — because some say chametz is called permitted; and some say winnowing basket since it emits immediately it is not via fire; and such is Magen Avraham note 37 in the name of Darkei Moshe in the name of Mahari Weil — they kasher a Pesach winnowing basket for the next year; and this is because b'dieved even in a chametz winnowing basket if one kashered — the matzah is not forbidden; see Magen Avraham note 37 further.
peri-megadim/22:_: Permitted [Taz] — he proved Yoreh De'ah 105 — a vessel of issur and permitted remained on it from above — does not forbid when did it absorb — after from above nitelaf it is; and this is the essence of the permission here in an earthenware barrel — hagalah does not help in holding beer many days — except from reason of nitelaf also; Magen Avraham siman 462 note 16. And Magen Avraham here note 40 and in Shach note 14 note 127 — he extended that all pickled issur from above absorbs and emits in whole; in other vessels hagalah helps — not pouring and we do not say like kli rishon in this; and in kli sheini hagalah does not help; and wine is different — see there; and the essence of permission is nat bar nat and nitelaf; and if they put vinegar in it — forbidden; and will be explained further below in this.
peri-megadim/23:_: Or via pouring [Taz]. I did not understand his holy words here because the meaning of his words z"l — therefore in kli sheini hagalah does not help because its absorption is great and does not emerge in hagalah in a short time and impossible to wait long to return and absorb like BY Tosefta seif 1; and for this reason pouring is superior for Chazal established it emits and does not absorb; and therefore pouring is superior unlike kli sheini in cold where absorption is slight hagalah is superior; if so why do we say the Torah testified that nothing of its orifices — ever kasher kli sheini in a large yorah that there are sixty against the water or Bach; and to permit like Tosefta note 2 — except that via hagalah never; and the same pouring all that was used in hot foods. And for the halacha per our view — even in cold all that waited from above — hagalah does not help and pouring is superior; and one does not learn leniency from wine; Peri Chadash note 14 note 127. And if new pottery that still did not satisfy to absorb — even for an hour it absorbs; see Taz siman 93 note 3; and old from above pickled absorbs and hagalah and pouring do not help; and here it deals with old for an hour or we do not hold thus. And pottery dried in a kiln — behold in sun has law of earthenware vessel — it has and is permitted in hagalah Magen Avraham note 4; and Magen Avraham wrote there.
peri-megadim/24:_: And hagalah [Taz] and see Levush and for adhesion hagalah does not help; and a beer barrel even opening one of its staves — not fit to kasher; and a honey barrel if opening one of its staves — permitted to kasher; and if he holds many days water — there is to side in this; see note 21.
peri-megadim/25:_: And b'dieved [Taz] — and we hold permitted absorption — nevertheless requires estimating against all of it in inserting a milking spoon and similarly; see in Bach in the name of Ravad z"l; and we hold requires against all of permitted; and Magen Avraham wrote in seif 4 note 8 — see there; and the general rule where there are many sides — one must combine also this that chametz is called permitted absorption. And the meaning of his words — even if they did not empty before Pesach — there is to permit on Pesach through nitelaf majority of permitters on Pesach; and in permitted absorption we say there are sixty and it is something and nitelaf; and nevertheless this that they are stringent even such as this; Magen Avraham wrote; and if they emptied before Pesach if they put vinegar in it and similarly — to rely to permit permitted absorption and that there were sixty — one does not rely on this in meat in milk and similarly; as stated; Peri Chadash — see there.
peri-megadim/26:_: But [Taz] — and if one kneaded in kneading chametz matzah without hagalah — Peri Chadash siman 462 note 19 and Levush here — it implies forbidden even though in other issurim if one kneaded in a forbidden vessel it does not emit without sharp pressure — kneading alone chametz the power of leavening in the vessel hastens to leaven the dough three hours in it. And Bach and Magen Avraham note 1 and the girsa in Shulchan Aruch — pottery vessel that was used as a leaven house — one shall not use matzah even in cold; and in Tur except in cold; and in Levush except in cold; and in Magen Avraham I explained. And behold a leaven house whose leavening is strong and absorbs in cold — it implies the same other issurim like leaven terumah or idol worship and similarly absorb in cold; and if afterward he baked it in hot foods — the matzah is forbidden like a peel applies — see in siman 105 and in Shach note 10; and even clean vessel and even in foods such as if the lower one was hot and absorbed issur of fat without gravy — possible we say since it already emitted it absorbs already cooled; and specifically b'eyna we say since it absorbed unlike clean vessel absorbed issur that has nothing to emit from its body — we say since it absorbed. And possible l'chatchila we are concerned for a leaven house; and b'dieved we say it did not absorb in cold a leaven house; see Levush; Magen Avraham wrote there hot matzah in chametz — some say permitted siman 461 seif 5 — forbids like nitelaf — it requires study; also from what is written matzah in hot in dry — it implies via gravy forbids in a vessel that absorbed leaven house that is sharp and very strong absorbs even without being forced. Peri Chadash wrote in Shulchan Aruch even in cold must be read except in cold — see there; Magen Avraham from this.
peri-megadim/27:א: But [Taz] and Magen Avraham notes 42 and 33 hold the Rambam relied here as Magen Avraham wrote there — the custom is like Rashi that hagalah does not help for a leaven house and the like like a mortar; but Taz holds where possible to libun they are stringent and we do not rely on the essence of the law that hagalah suffices; and wood siman 462 because impossible to scrape etc.; therefore Rambam wrote there mortar of wood — peel and hagalah because we are concerned for grooves — this is not wood that impossible libun suffices l'chatchila in hagalah; and support for Taz z"l; Peri Chadash note 60; and per Magen Avraham it works out. And Magen Avraham wrote in a barrel of wine — one does not kasher it unless he cooked in water and ashes — see there likewise Levush in seif 61 — worse than leaven house and charoset; and possible b'dieved even if they kashered without water and ashes first — one does not forbid b'dieved what was placed inside; siman 462 in water and ashes — one does not kasher Magen Avraham note 10 — except afterward one kashered.
peri-megadim/27:ב: And Mishnah Berurah in responsum siman 58 in Yeshiva on Pesach that requires pouring and a barrel breaking; and Rashba note 44 and Peri Chadash note 24 wrote he holds a barrel requires breaking — it is like chametz b'eyna; and possible the language is imprecise; and furthermore this is during Pesach; but after Pesach permitted via hagalah — so in Rashba; and Peri Chadash concluded via rinsing or hagalah; and in my view it appears our rabbis z"l thought very deeply in this; and this is the matter we spoke in Magen Avraham note 1 — certainly vessels that absorbed chametz before Pesach — permitted to leave them and use after Pesach like Rashi; and therefore l"sh penalty not common in your hand unlike a vessel that absorbed during Pesach chametz of Israel b'eyna — and we hold a vessel that absorbed d'rabbanan issur even Bach forbidden to use in it ab initio; and as Magen Avraham wrote in Peri Megadim Yoreh De'ah; and I resolved there as the house guardian z"l wrote — after Pesach l"sh to decree lest ab initio; see there; and if so in Yeshiva where nitelaf does not help — stronger than wine like BY siman 462 Taz note 4 and siman 462 in Magen Avraham note 25; and here note 40 — if so if absorbed during Pesach wine of Israel in a barrel — forbidden after Pesach through rinsing also hagalah does not help because it returns and absorbs; and l"sh Bach and nat bar nat because it is sharp; and in a large yorah there are sixty against it — possible otherwise; except wine possible for its taste he did and not nullified excessively in sixty and absorbed in the barrel; see in Tosefta Magen Avraham note 1; barrel that they hold vinegar kosher even before Pesach — nat bar nat does not help; see there.
peri-megadim/27:ג: Here is what we wrote — wine for its taste acts; and if wine fell until the night into cooked food that has sixty — forbidden because presumption and nat bar nat in a thousand; and now I saw in responsum Chavot Yair z"l siman 20 at end of the responsum s.v. umemeila etc. — it is like spices in a thousand — not nullified; and possible via ashes one is permitted to kasher after Pesach as Taz wrote here not in the eye; as stated.
peri-megadim/27:ד: And there is to examine a matter — for its taste acts — it is not nullified if mixed in its kind if we decree lest it is not its kind; and per the Mechaber for its taste — therefore not nullified — it appears thus; and per d'rabbanan all this — possible to be lenient even d'rabbanan issur we decree lest it is not its kind in moist food; and nevertheless such as this possible more than sixty to be lenient; see note 99; and the matters are long.
peri-megadim/27:ה: And Magen Avraham wrote in responsum Chavot Yair z"l there — the malt that changed its taste since they uprooted to make wine — it is like very moldy fruits that are not fit at all for eating and they are eaten via sugar and honey — in their language they remain for every matter — see there. Siman 204 seif 5 and seif 14 to divide between intentional planting thus or not — see there; and if so barley beer and wine — one blesses shehakol if we say the malt changed its taste and is not fit at all thus for eating; and it appears since they were fit initially only via work — changed all that was fit afterward like initially it is; and therefore they needed to give taste why one blesses on beer shehakol; and the matters are long. And still it requires study — chametz that was disqualified from human food entirely and was restored afterward via mixture and similarly — if one is liable lashes and karet for it; siman 462 in Mishnah Berurah; and Magen Avraham wrote there.
